Few things I noticed and my own theories:

- The words Hamelin had Rebecca say were the names of demons, but phonetically spelled with commonly known words so Rebecca (and her father) wouldn't catch on. The demons actual names, if I'm right, is Paimon, Bael (or Baal), and Balam. It's possible one of these demons are who talked to Rebecca on her headset. 

- There's a great number of references to Balam on the farm video, considering that Balam has body parts from a snake, ram, and a bull while riding a bear. He also has flaming eyes (probably why the barn has bloodshot eyes) and a hoarse voice. It's possible it was Balam watching over Amanda/Rebecca in the farm video, but I'm not sure.

- There's a chance the reason why the demon Amanda (idk what to call that thing) can sneak around is cause Balam and Baal/Bael has the power of invisibility. 

- There's a few references to Bael (or Baal) too: he's been shown as having spider legs and with the head of a cat, he also has powers of invisibility and a hoarse voice, he has a similar amount of knowledge of things like Paimon, and has the power to increase popularity. 

- There's also a great number of references to Paimon, such as how Amanda asks questions you must get correctly, how Amanda teaches from a great number of subjects, Amanda wanting to share secrets, the appearance/disappearance of random objects, and random objects coming to life (Paimon can reanimate the dead and give familiars).

- For the contract signing video, my guess is that they made Rebecca an orphan by disappearing her father so there wouldn't be any impediments to getting her to sign a contract. It's highly illegal to have a minor sign anything without parental oversight.

- Considering the demons above, Wooly is potentially a familiar from Paimon created to control Rebecca while stuck in Amanda's form. I think that's also why the eyes on demon Amanda look like Wooly's wool - to show how the demon isn't necessarily Amanda/Rebecca but something controlled by another.

My main theory is that the contract Rebecca signed meant Rebecca signed her soul to Hamelin - which is how she became a perpetual tv show host: they weren't getting her to say words for AI voice recognition for an AI hosted show, they were getting her to say demon names to summon a demon to sell her soul to for the show's continued success and to trap her soul into the show itself. As for which demon has her soul? I'm not sure, there's a chance she was sacrificed to all of them or deals were made with all of them.

comments.text:
For Cory and those confused: Hamelin was a town that hired a man (later to be referred to as the Pied Piper of Hamelin) to use his flute in order to get rid of the rats that infested and overrun their town. When he did what he was asked to do, the townsfolk cheated him out of the reward, so as a means of exacting revenge, the Pied Piper came back later that same year and led the children of the town away from their houses with his flute, and depending on the version you read, he either led them through a portal, drowned them in the river of Weser, or led them into a cave to kill them. This explains why the Hameln logo is a rat, why there's a rat running around in game, and why the children are hypnotized upon starting up the show (there most likely is a hypnotizing aspect to the Hameln opening music). The fact that their slogan is "follow us to fun" just further proves the theory. What Hameln does with the kids is debatable, though I believe they are using the kids for something demonic, because Rebecca says the names of demons Bael, Paimon, and Balam three times to summon them.

Additional info I forgot to add: supposedly, there is a stone facade of the "Pied Pipers" house, which has the inscriptions, “A.D. 1284 – on the 26th of June – the day of St John and St Paul – 130 children – born in Hamelin – were led out of the town by a piper wearing multicoloured clothes. After passing the Calvary near the [sic] Koppenberg they disappeared forever". The details here might have a correlation with the story, such as the time during the light blue tape at 3:06 saying 2;48, which is the scrambled version of when this supposedly occurred, that being 1284 AD. Although this is obvious, this probably means Hameln was dishonest about their business with Sam and Rebecca Colton, and cheated them out of the reward they promised when making Amanda the Adventurer into a cartoon show. I'll edit again when I find more info.

Fun fact bc I dont think anyone pointed this out yet: Hameln Company, the in-game animation studio for Amanda the Adventurer, is FOR SURE in reference to the Pied Piper of Hamelin story. For those who don't know or need a refresher: the story takes place in Hameln, Germany (frequently spelled 'Hamelin' in English adaptations) in a town infested by rats and mice. A piper had been passing through, and he arranged to take care of the vermin problem with an expected payment. With his magic flute, he hypnotized all the rodents in the town and led them down to the river where they drowned. Despite doing his job to the fullest, the town suddenly decided they didn't want to pay him after all. So as revenge, the pied piper came again the next day and hypnotized nearly all the town children with his magic flute, leading them out of the town and never to be seen again. 

The fact that Hameln's company logo uses the shape of a mouse can be no coincidence. Theory: the company is using Rebecca (ie Amanda) as a scapegoat to play the role of the piper, having her recite strange readings as if to invoke a spell that would have effect over the show's target audience. Children are later reported to go MISSING when watching the show. As to where, we don't know. There may be a strong possibility that Hameln is somehow stealing children for neferious means. 'Young blood' sacrifices maybe?


Another theory is that the guy who pops in at the very end of the last ending Cory got could be Sam Colt, making a return after going 'missing.' It could also be some kind of Pied Piper stand-in, sent by Hameln to go after the player. Some say it might be Aunt Kate herself. Whatever the case, Cory remains the goat for hunting for all the endings and secrets this game could have. Love ya vids, dude!
